# History

Topics in the **History** category of the *the country japan* knowledge base.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: category-index — maintained by build-structure; do not edit by hand -->
| Topic | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| [Edo Period](edo-period.md) | The 264-year Tokugawa shogunate (1603–1867) — an era of enforced peace, *sakoku* isolation, rigid feudal hierarchy, and a flourishing urban culture that laid the foundations of modern Japan. |
| [Meiji Restoration](meiji-restoration.md) | The 1868 transformation from feudal shogunate to modernized nation-state that prevented colonization and positioned Japan among the great powers. |
| [Sengoku Period](sengoku-period.md) | The era of civil warfare (1467–1615) following the fall of the Ashikaga shogunate, during which regional *daimyo* competed until the great unifiers consolidated Japan. |
| [World War II](world-war-ii.md) | Japan's imperial expansion, alliance with the Axis, the Pacific War (1941–1945), the atomic bombings, and the 1945 surrender that ended imperial militarism and opened the Allied occupation. |
| [Heian Period](heian-period.md) | Japan's classical era (794–1185)—the founding of Heian-kyō, the Fujiwara regency, the *kana* literary flowering of *The Tale of Genji*, and the rise of the warrior clans that ended aristocratic rule. |
| [Taishō Period](taisho-period.md) | The era of social transformation (1912–1926) between Meiji modernization and Shōwa militarism—"Taishō democracy," universal male suffrage (1925), Western-influenced mass culture, and the 1923 Great Kantō Earthquake. |
| [Kamakura Period](kamakura-period.md) | Japan's first warrior government (1185–1333)—the Minamoto shogunate and Hōjō regency, the *Jōei Shikimoku* legal code, the spread of Zen and Pure Land Buddhism, and the repulse of the Mongol invasions that laid the foundations of samurai rule. |
| [Russo-Japanese War](russo-japanese-war.md) | The 1904–1905 conflict in which Japan defeated Russia—the sieges of Port Arthur and the annihilation of the Baltic Fleet at Tsushima—establishing itself as the first modern non-Western great power and reshaping the balance of power in East Asia. |
| [Genpei War](genpei-war.md) | The 1180–1185 civil war between the Minamoto and Taira clans that ended Heian court dominance, established Japan's first military government under Yoritomo at Kamakura, and inaugurated seven centuries of samurai rule. |
| [Azuchi-Momoyama Period](azuchi-momoyama-period.md) | The unification era (1568–1603) of the three unifiers—Oda Nobunaga, Toyotomi Hideyoshi, and Tokugawa Ieyasu—marked by grand castle architecture, the Kanō school and *wabi-cha*, Portuguese contact and the Korean invasions, and the consolidation that produced the Tokugawa peace. |
| [Nara Period](nara-period.md) | Japan's first permanent capital era (710–794) at Heijō-kyō—a Chinese-style *ritsuryō* bureaucratic state, the Tōdai-ji Great Buddha and provincial temple network, and the *Kojiki*, *Nihon Shoki*, and *Man'yōshū* that founded the written tradition. |
